youtube.title: Ramayana · Bala Kanda Part 1: Rama's First Battle
youtube.description:
His father said he was too young to fight rakshasas. On the sixth day, they came.
For six days and nights Rama and Lakshmana had guarded a sage's sacred fire without sleep, and now the rakshasas swept down like monsoon clouds. 🔥

Bala Kanda Part 1 tells the opening of Valmiki's Ramayana as one continuous chalk-animated story. It begins on the bank of the Tamasa, where a hunter's arrow and a grieving krauncha bird move the sage Valmiki to speak the first shloka. Then comes King Dasharatha's long wait for sons, the payasa from the sacred fire and the birth of the four princes; the sage Vishvamitra at the palace gate, asking for Rama; Tataka's ruined forest and the gift of the divine weapons; and six sleepless days and nights guarding the sacrifice at Siddhashrama. It ends on the road toward Mithila, where a bow waits that no god could string.

📜 Verses on screen (Valmiki Ramayana, vulgate, southern recension):
VR 1.1.2 (vulgate) · ko nv asmin sāmprataṃ loke · Valmiki's question to Narada
VR 1.2.15 (vulgate) · mā niṣāda pratiṣṭhāṃ tvam · the first shloka
VR 1.16.27 (vulgate) · kausalyāyai narapatiḥ · the king shares the payasa
VR 1.20.2 (vulgate) · ūnaṣoḍaśavarṣo me · not yet sixteen
VR 1.23.2 (vulgate) · kausalyā suprajā rāma · the dawn call
VR 1.25.18 (vulgate) · nṛśaṃsam anṛśaṃsaṃ vā · the duty of those who protect
VR 1.28.2 (vulgate) · gṛhītāstro'smi bhagavan · how to call the weapons back
VR 1.30.20 (vulgate) · paśya lakṣmaṇa śīteṣuṃ · the Manava weapon spares a life
VR 1.31.9 (vulgate) · nāsya devā na gandharvā · the bow no god could string

Later tradition: the Venkatesha Suprabhatam (composed 1420–1432 CE) opens with VR 1.23.2.
Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda, sargas 1–31 (vulgate, southern recension)
